107.prompt:
Edit the supplied two transparent 2D character animation reference images to paint ONE new intermediate BODY-ONLY sprite for landing into running, called pose A. The first reference (male-89.png) is the crouched landing body immediately before pose A; the second reference (male-48.png) is the run entry several frames later. This is a supplemental animation drawing, not a new character design. Preserve precisely the original body's compact chibi proportions, limb lengths, perspective facing screen right, smooth shaded cartoon brushwork, dark clean outlines, and the SAME teal short-sleeve collared button shirt, olive khaki long trousers with brown waistband, and white rounded shoes. Do not introduce new costume details or change sleeve thickness, shoe design or limb thickness.

CRITICAL LAYER REQUIREMENT: Output ONLY the body from the short neck stump/collar DOWN through the shoes, including both arms and hands, on a true transparent background. Do NOT draw ANY head, scalp, face, eyes, ears, hair, or floating head fragment. The existing approved head will be rigidly composited later from the original frame. All of the upper portion of the canvas above the neck must be empty transparent. Do not fill that space with anything.

COMPOSITION AND PLACEMENT: Same 512 x 768 portrait animation cell coordinate system as the references. Do not crop the canvas or center/enlarge the body. All coordinates below are measured in that 512 x 768 cell (if output at 2x, double every coordinate). Preserve large empty transparent head area at top. The collar opening / neck attachment is approximately at (285,453). The body's top shoulder silhouette begins around y=425 and neck stump must be short and naturally connect into this collar. Keep all body details at the same scale as the reference.

POSE A — WEIGHT TRANSFER AT END OF LANDING: Pelvis/hip center at (242,568). Body is still low with slightly bent knees and a slight forward lean, halfway between the two references. Do not stand fully upright. The far leg is the screen-right leg in the first reference: it now takes most of the body weight. Far supporting shoe center approximately (262,680), its sole lowest y approximately 695, firmly planted. Near leg is screen-left in first reference: near knee (240,612); near shoe toe (242,697) retains its last ground contact as heel starts lifting to push off. Keep a readable separation of the two leg silhouettes with correct far-leg occlusion. This is a tiny natural forward weight transfer, not a large new step or a jump. Both thighs and calves retain the same volumes.

ARMS: Keep elbows bent as in reference 89. Near wrist (225,522), near fist gently drawn back by the torso; far front fist center (346,516). The front fist remains in front, the other arm stays back. Do not drop or straighten the arms. Maintain close correspondence of shirt sleeve outlines, forearm volumes, and hands with reference images. Maintain the collar, shirt hem and trouser waist as one coherent clothing connection, without doubled lines, holes or discontinuities.

Render a single high-quality, crisp, full-resolution transparent body layer. No background, no ground, no cast shadow, no checkerboard pixels, no guides, no labels, no text, no ruler, no arrows, no second character, no side-by-side sheet. This image is just the one body patch in its correct location in the 512x768 cell, and the upper head region is entirely transparent.
